question: If a right circular cone of height 24 cm has the circumference of its base 42 π cm, then the volume of the cone is (use π = (22)/(7)).
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The **radius (r)** is calculated from the **circumference**: 2πr = 42π ⇒ r = 21 cm.

Using the **volume formula** for a **cone**: V = (1/3) × π × r² × h.

Substitute values: V = (1/3) × (22/7) × 21 × 21 × 24.

V = 22 × 21 × 24 = 11088 cm³.

**∴ The correct answer is 11088 cm³.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Height (h)** of the cone = 24 cm

**Circumference** of the base = 42π cm

**Formula Used:**

Circumference of circle = 2πr

**Volume of a cone** = (1/3)πr²h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6470df65df6b9171c9606d045951060d8abd8918faf533d544505e3a50db7b3b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2 × π × r = 42π

⇒ 2r = 42

⇒ r = 21 cm

⇒ **Volume** = (1/3) × (22/7) × 21 × 21 × 24

⇒ Volume = (1/3) × 22 × 3 × 21 × 24

⇒ Volume = 22 × 21 × 24

⇒ Volume = 462 × 24

⇒ Volume = 11088 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 11088 cm³.**

**__Additional Information__**

Slant Height of a Cone

The slant height (l) is the distance from the apex to any point on the base circumference: l = √(r² + h²).

Curved Surface Area (CSA)

The area of the curved surface of a cone is given by the formula: CSA = πrl.

Total Surface Area (TSA)

The total surface area includes the base area and the curved area: TSA = πr(l + r).

Relation with Cylinder

The volume of a cone is exactly one-third the volume of a cylinder with the same radius and height.</p
